title: 7 Best Neighborhoods in Denver for Every Lifestyle
summary: Discover top Denver neighborhoods for families, professionals, retirees, and outdoor enthusiasts.
body_markdown:
Free image via[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/denver-colorado-mountains-city-2228782/)


**Denver Neighborhoods: Quick Facts**


**7 Best Neighborhoods in Denver**


**Finding the Right Denver Neighborhood for You**


The mountains are never far from view in Denver. On clear days, the Front Range provides a dramatic backdrop that gives Denver a truly unique feel. Easy access to the outdoors, combined with a lively urban scene, means there’s no shortage of things to do in Denver. This appealing combination continues to attract new residents, and as a result, the Denver metro area has grown by[nearly 3%](https://denverite.com/2025/03/27/denver-metro-population-growth/) between 2020 and 2024.


But living in Denver can feel completely different from one neighborhood to the next. Some areas boast walkable restaurant districts and historic homes, while others offer quieter streets, larger properties, and quick access to parks and trails. In this guide to the best neighborhoods in Denver, we’ll cover some of the top places to live, depending on your lifestyle.


## Denver Neighborhoods: Quick Facts


Here’s a snapshot of important facts to know about Denver neighborhoods.


- Denver has[78 recognized neighborhoods](https://denverarchitecture.org/resources/neighborhood-listing/) .
- The typical home value in Denver is about[$539,712](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/11093/denver-co/) .
- The average rent in Denver is roughly[$1,634 per month](https://www.apartments.com/rent-market-trends/denver-co/) .
- West Denver neighborhoods offer quicker access to the mountains.
- RiNo, LoDo, and Capitol Hill top the list of best neighborhoods in Denver for young professionals.
- Washington Park and Central Park are among the best neighborhoods in Denver for families.
- Cherry Creek and Hilltop are some of the wealthiest neighborhoods in Denver.


Our neighborhood list includes information on home values, commute times, and character, so you can decide which neighborhood is the best fit for you as you explore living in Denver.


## 7 Best Neighborhoods in Denver


Denver neighborhoods feel surprisingly different from one another. The best neighborhood in Denver for you ultimately comes down to factors like your lifestyle, budget, commute times, and personal priorities.


### 1. Washington Park: Best Overall Neighborhood


- **Average Home Value:**[$1.2 M](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/268772/washington-park-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,710](https://www.apartments.com/washington-park-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 10–15-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Active, upscale, relaxed


Washington Park typically tops the list of best neighborhoods in Denver because it balances city living with access to green space, such as the massive 155-acre[Washington Park](https://visitdenver.com/listing/washington-park/6828/) , which serves as the neighborhood’s centerpiece. Here, locals flock on weekends to run, bike, paddleboard, or simply walk the trails around the lakes.


Historic homes, small apartment buildings, coffee shops, and local restaurants line the surrounding streets. South Gaylord Street and nearby Pearl Street, in particular, offer residents plenty of dining and shopping options without having to head downtown.


### 2. RiNo: Best Neighborhood for Young Professionals


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/photo-of-friends-smiling-in-a-pub-7022164/)


- **Median Home Price:**[$487,500](https://www.homes.com/denver-co/river-north-neighborhood/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,946](https://www.apartments.com/rino-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 5–10-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Creative, energetic, modern


River North Art District, better known as RiNo, is often considered the coolest neighborhood in Denver. This very walkable area is where a creative art scene meets craft breweries. Former warehouses are now home to art galleries, cocktail bars, coffee roasters, music venues, and some of the best restaurants in Denver.


The neighborhood is also close to Downtown and Union Station, making it one of the best Denver neighborhoods for professionals seeking a convenient commute and an active social scene. Areas like[Larimer Square](https://visitdenver.com/things-to-do/attractions/larimer-square/) stay busy well into the evening, especially on weekends.


### 3. Central Park: Best Neighborhood for Families


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/happy-family-sitting-together-in-front-of-house-7982544/)


- **Average Home Value:**[$764,111](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/275564/central-park-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,774](https://www.apartments.com/central-park-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 20–25-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Residential, family-friendly, spacious


Central Park is popular with families who want to stay close to Downtown but need a little more room. Centered around the 80-acre Central Park, the neighborhood was designed with families in mind, featuring 50 parks, 7 pools, a recreation center, and the Denver Public Library. Housing options include a mix of single-family homes as well as duplexes, townhomes, condos, and apartments.


While the area is situated eight miles from Downtown, the neighborhood offers plenty of everyday city amenities, with schools, grocery stores, coffee shops, and restaurants all within easy reach. And if you’re looking to venture outside the area, it’s also well connected by Central Park Station, which offers commuter rail and bus service to both Downtown Denver and Denver International Airport.


### 4. Cherry Creek: Wealthiest Neighborhood in Denver


- **Average Home Value:**[$1.2M](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/268635/cherry-creek-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$2,394](https://www.apartments.com/cherry-creek-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 10-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Polished, upscale, walkable


It’s easy to see why Cherry Creek has a reputation as one of the richest neighborhoods in Denver. Luxury condos sit a few blocks away from large homes on quiet tree-lined streets, while the neighborhood’s shopping and restaurant scene draws people from across the city. Even though it’s close to Downtown, parts of Cherry Creek feel surprisingly residential once you get away from the main commercial corridors.


The[Cherry Creek Shopping Center](https://www.simon.com/mall/cherry-creek-shopping-center) and the surrounding business district attract residents who prefer walkability without living directly Downtown. It’s also one of the nicest neighborhoods in Denver for professionals who want easy access to both downtown offices and outdoor recreation.


### 5. Sloan’s Lake: Best Neighborhood for Outdoor Enthusiasts


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/sunset-silhouette-of-cyclist-by-lake-32877476/)


- **Average Home Value:**[$810,422](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/403512/sloan-lake-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,724](https://www.apartments.com/sloan-lake-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 10–15-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Scenic, active, laid-back


Sloan’s Lake is one of the best places to live in Denver if you love nature. It contains the city’s largest lake and park system. The nearly 3-mile loop around the lake attracts runners, cyclists, paddleboarders, and dog walkers year-round.


It’s more relaxed than RiNo or LoDo but still has plenty of restaurants and rooftop bars. The balance between outdoor access and nearness to Downtown is a big plus for many residents.


### 6. Capitol Hill: Best Neighborhood for Nightlife


- **Average Home Value:**[$317,027](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/268628/capitol-hill-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,395](https://www.apartments.com/capitol-hill-denver-co/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 5-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Dense, eclectic, historic


Capitol Hill offers some of the most urban living in Denver. Apartment buildings, historic mansions, coffee shops, and late-night restaurants all occupy a relatively compact area near Downtown, making it the[most walkable neighborhood in Denver](https://www.walkscore.com/CO/Denver/Capitol_Hill) .


The area South of Colfax Avenue (SoCo) is known for its nightlife, with a mix of music venues, nightclubs, and bars in a highly walkable setting. Other neighborhood attractions, such as[Civic Center Park](https://civiccenterpark.org/) and the[Denver Art Museum](https://www.denverartmuseum.org/en) , are also easily reachable on foot.


### 7. Platt Park: Best Neighborhood for Retirees


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/photo-of-an-elderly-couple-sitting-together-on-concrete-steps-7729132/)


- **Average Home Value:**[$838,032](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/268720/platt-park-denver-co/)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,891](https://www.rentcafe.com/average-rent-market-trends/us/co/denver/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 15-minute drive
- **Vibe:** Charming, pleasant, community-focused


If you’d like to retire to a small-town lifestyle without giving up big-city amenities, consider Platt Park.[South Pearl Street](https://www.southpearlstreet.com/) is the neighborhood’s hub, with restaurants, coffee shops, bars, and a busy farmers market on weekends. Mature trees, historic homes, and the offerings of South Pearl Street give the neighborhood a sense of character and an established feel that many newer Denver communities lack.


Nearby light rail access makes it a breeze to get around without driving through central Denver. And Washington Park, with its lovely green space and lakes, is only a few minutes away.


## Finding the Right Denver Neighborhood for You


The best neighborhoods in Denver all have something unique to offer. Choose the location that best suits your lifestyle, whether that’s Capitol Hill with its bustling nightlife or Sloan’s Lake with its convenient access to nature.
